title: Mandala — three rounds
subtitle: A flat 14 cm circle with six-stitch increases and a shell finishing round — the entry point for mandala work
excerpt: The three-round mandala is a flat circle built from six-stitch increases per round in double crochet, with a shell round at round 3 that gives the radiating petal effect. At 14 cm diameter in DK cotton on a 4 mm hook, it works as a coaster, a bag base, or the central panel in a larger mandala project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A circle that lies flat without cupping or ruffling. In crochet, a flat circle in double crochet requires six increases per round — one at each of six evenly-spaced points. More increases per round causes ruffling; fewer causes cupping.

Multiple trebles worked into the same stitch or space, fanning outward to create a shell or petal shape. In the three-round mandala, a shell of three trebles sits at each of the six increase points of the previous round.

content.text: The three-round mandala is a
flat-circle
built from six-stitch increases per round in double crochet, with a
shell

round at round 3 that gives the radiating petal effect. This is the entry point for mandala work: the shape stays flat, the increases are consistent, and the shell round establishes the pattern that the more complex versions extend.

At 14 cm diameter in DK cotton on a 4 mm hook, the three-round mandala works as a coaster, a bag base, or a standalone decorative panel. The shell round reads as six radiating petals, which is the visual language all the larger mandalas develop from this foundation.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton in one to three colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished three-round mandala measures 14 cm diameter in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-block. Make a test motif before starting a large project — flat-circle work is more sensitive to hook size than cluster work.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; called single crochet (sc) in US patterns.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Place a stitch marker in the first stitch of each round to keep track of the round boundary. Do not turn.
Round 1
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. Work 6 dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 dc.)
Round 2
Ch 1. Work 2 dc into each stitch around. Sl st to first dc to join. (12 dc.)
Round 3

Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Into the same stitch work 2 tr. *Ch 2, skip 1 st, 3 tr into next st*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (6 shells of 3 tr, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Rounds 1 and 2 show flat-circle double crochet; round 3 shows the six treble shell groups separated by chain-2 spaces.

definition.title: Mandala — three rounds
definition.caption: Three rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 and 2 flat-circle double crochet with six-stitch increases per round. Round 3: six radiating treble shell groups of 3tr each, separated by ch-2 spaces.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Thread through a tapestry needle and weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side of round 3, reverse direction through 2 to 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail along round 1. Steam-block flat on a blocking mat — pin each of the six shell groups to keep the petal shape even.
Joining

The three-round mandala does not tile edge-to-edge like a square or hexagon — it is a circle, so joining into a flat fabric requires fill-in motifs or a joining row. As a standalone coaster or bag base, it needs no joining. For a blanket, join through the chain-2 spaces of adjacent shell rounds with a flat slip-stitch seam, and fill gaps with small treble triangles.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a delicates cycle. Lay flat to dry, re-blocking the circle shape if the shell round has shifted during washing.
What to try next

The five-round mandala continues the same flat-circle base for two more rounds before the shell edging, giving a 20 cm diameter motif suited to a bag base or small wall piece. The eight-round version reaches 30 cm and introduces V-stitches in the later rounds for additional texture.
